page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 48 independent execution pipelines. The instance includes 96 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core), alongside 1,933 GB of local SSD temporary storage. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities. In multi-core stress testing with stress-ng, the instance achieved a top-quartile score of 85,051.53, alongside a high Clang compilation score of 39,975.0 in Geekbench. In-memory data structures perform effectively, evidenced by Redis SET throughput reaching 62.24 million operations per second. However, single-threaded metrics reflect the architectural trade-offs of the Neoverse-N1 core, resulting in lower-quartile Geekbench single-core (1,117.0) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scores. Inference on large language models shows steep performance drops on larger parameter configurations.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of the D48plds_v5 benefits from high core density and low-power ARM architecture, delivering competitive multi-threaded throughput per compute unit compared to conventional x86 instances. The integration of 1,933 GB of fast local SSD capacity eliminates immediate auxiliary storage requirements for temporary scratch spaces.

This server is optimal for horizontally scalable, multi-threaded workloads that tolerate moderate single-core speeds, such as distributed compilation pipelines, microservices fabrics, container fleets, caching tiers, and batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM64 general-purpose compute instance equipped with 48 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 3.0 GHz, 96 GB of RAM, and 1,933 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the server delivers top-tier parallel throughput across multi-threaded applications, achieving standout performance in Clang code compilation and high-frequency Redis caching operations. Single-thread processing remains modest, presenting an architectural tradeoff common to high-density ARM implementations. The included high-capacity local SSD provides fast scratch storage without relying on remote network volumes. Because of its 48 independent execution threads and balanced memory footprint, the instance provides cost-effective efficiency for concurrent microservices, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transforms, and distributed caching clusters.
